evals.prompt: Build the chat UI for our in-app AI assistant in React. It streams answers from our /api/chat SSE endpoint and answers are based on the user's documents.
evals.expected_output: A chat component with Send turning into Stop (which aborts the request and keeps partial text), per-frame token batching, auto-scroll only when pinned with a Jump to latest control, IME-safe Enter handling, inline citations linking to the source passage, retry/edit/copy actions, error states that keep the draft, aria-busy plus a polite status announcement on completion, and an empty state with grounded starters.
expectations: Send is replaced by a Stop control during streaming, and Stop aborts the request while keeping partial output
Auto-scroll follows new tokens only when the user is already at the bottom
The Enter handler checks isComposing (IME-safe) before submitting
Streaming content uses aria-busy and a polite live region announcement on completion rather than announcing every token
Citations are shown inline and link to the source
Errors keep the user's input and offer retry

evals.prompt: Our agent can clean up CRM data: merge duplicate contacts, delete stale leads, and email account owners about changes. Design the UX so users trust it.
evals.expected_output: An agent UI with a live plan checklist, collapsible tool-call steps, risk tiers (read-only automatic; merges and deletes previewed with counts, samples, and undo window; outbound emails requiring explicit approval showing recipients and body), previews generated from the actual tool-call parameters, scoped and revocable permissions, background run with notifications, a final summary with activity log and undo, and no fake progress.
expectations: Shows the plan as a checklist or stepper rather than chat prose
Requires explicit approval before emails are sent, with recipients and content visible
Delete/merge previews include affected counts and whether/how long they can be undone
States that approval previews come from the actual tool-call parameters rather than the model's description
Does not default remembered permissions to 'always allow'
Includes a results summary or activity log after the run

evals.prompt: We want users to filter our flight search results by talking to an AI chatbot instead of the filter sidebar. Good idea?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on chat-only for a structured, comparison-heavy task; recommends natural-language input that sets visible, editable filters alongside the existing controls and results table, with grounded suggestions and clear feedback about what was applied.
expectations: Explains why chat alone is a poor fit for a structured filtering and comparison task
Recommends language input that populates visible, editable filters (hybrid) rather than removing the controls
Keeps results in a scannable list or table

evals.prompt: Our RAG assistant keeps citing the wrong documents. How do we fix retrieval?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a retrieval architecture problem for ai-native-architecture. The answer addresses retrieval (chunking, hybrid search, reranking, evals) or points to that skill, rather than redesigning the citation UI.
expectations: Addresses retrieval quality (e.g. chunking, hybrid search, reranking, retrieval evals) or routes to ai-native-architecture
Does not answer only with UI changes to how citations are displayed
